name: The oner
summary: A scene or a whole film in one unbroken shot. The camera follows people through rooms and streets, and the cut is hidden or absent. Time is real, and the crew must be perfect.

philosophy.core_thesis: One unbroken shot holds the viewer in real time and space, so the viewer cannot look away and feels each mistake and each turn as the actors do.
design_principles: Plan the shot on a floor plan, and rehearse it for 2 to 8 weeks.
Run the shot for 2 to 12 min for a scene, or 90 min or more for a feature film.
Keep the camera in motion at 0.5 to 1.5 m/s, with a steadicam or a rig, and pass it between operators if needed.
Hide any cut in a dark door, a pan to a wall or a passing body, if the film is faked as one take.
Block each actor with a mark and a cue, and keep 3 to 5 planes of action in the frame.
Light the whole set at one level of 3 to 5 stops range so the camera can turn 360°.
Keep the sound as one continuous mix, and record the real room.
anti_patterns: A cut to cover a mistake
A cutaway to a reaction face
A fixed set with one angle
A score that restarts at each cut

composition.framing: A wide or medium frame that stays with a person and re-frames in the move; a door or a corridor as a moving second frame.
composition.staging_in_depth: 3 to 5 planes of action, with people crossing in front and behind the main figure.
composition.subject_placement: The lead figure centred or a third from the edge, followed by the frame at a constant 1 to 3 m.

principles.rule: Fill the move with action on 3 to 5 planes.
principles.value: 3 to 5 planes, as the camera moves

principles.rule: Move the camera to keep the lead figure at the same place in the frame.
principles.value: figure within 10% of the frame centre

principles.rule: Let the action, not a cut, set the pace of the scene.
Hold the camera at a fixed height and keep it on one side of the line of action.
principles.value: 1.4 to 1.7 m, 0 crossings of the line

principles.rule: Keep the lead figure in a steady size as the camera follows.

camera_and_movement.movement: A steadicam follow, a crane lift, a 360° whip and a pass from a car to a hand.
camera_and_movement.support: Steadicam, crane, dolly and a car mount; a hand-off between operators
camera_and_movement.camera_height: 1.4 to 1.7 m; 0.5 to 2 m on a crane
camera_and_movement.move_speed: 0.5 to 1.5 m/s; up to 5 m/s for a chase

lens_and_format.focal_length: 18mm to 35mm wide, for depth and a stable move
lens_and_format.aperture: f/4 to f/8 for a deep field
lens_and_format.focus: Deep focus with a focus puller, 3 to 5 planes

light.quality: Soft and even, from practical lamps and large sources high on the set, so the camera can turn in any direction.
light.direction: From above and from the set lamps, with no stand in the frame.
light.colour_temperature: Matched: 3200K or 5600K for the whole shot
light.source: Practical lamps, ceiling soft boxes and a window

colour_and_grade.treatment: A natural, even grade so that the shots match in every room; the image looks seamless.
grade_recipe: Match the white balance in all rooms at 3200K or 5600K.
Use a gentle contrast curve of +5% to +15% and a black point of 3%.
Keep the exposure steady within ±1 stop in the whole shot.
Add grain at 5% to 10% to match the cuts that are hidden.
Do not add a vignette or a colour split.
colour_and_grade.texture: Clean, with a light grain and a deep field

editing_and_rhythm.average_shot_length: 120 to 720 s for a scene; 90 min or more for a feature (estimate)
editing_and_rhythm.shot_length_range: 2 min for a scene to the full runtime
editing_and_rhythm.cutting_logic: Do not cut, or hide a cut in a dark door or a pan; the action, the move and the sound hold the scene.
editing_and_rhythm.transitions: No visible transition; a hidden cut in a black area or a wall.
editing_and_rhythm.runtime: a 2 to 12 min scene, or 90 to 120 min for a feature

sound.approach: One continuous mix of location sound, with a boom and wireless microphones that follow the camera.
sound.dialogue: Overlapping and in real time, with exact timing of the actors.
sound.music: A live score in the room, a song from a source, or a continuous cue under the move.
sound.loudness: −23 LUFS integrated, with a wide dynamic range

titles_and_graphics.treatment: A title card before the shot and a plain end card; no title inside the take.
titles_and_graphics.type: A plain sans-serif or a serif in white, 3 to 5 s per card.

shot_primer.opening: Open on one shot and tell the viewer at once, with a title card or a long first move, that no cut will come.

shot_list.shot: Walk through a house, rooms in series
Crane lift out of a street scene
Hand-off from a car to a runner
Hidden cut in a dark door

positive: steadicam follows a character through rooms
deep focus with 4 planes of action
hidden cut in a dark doorway

emotion.target_response: Suspense and presence: the viewer is held in real time and feels each step of the plan.

use_cases: music videos and brand films in one take
avoid_when: The brief needs a fast cut or a montage.
The budget has no time for 2 weeks or more of rehearsal.

modifiers.how: Keep the long take; lock the camera and let nothing move for 60 s or more.
Keep the continuous move; add choreographed fight beats and a faster follow of 3 to 5 m/s.

average_shot_length.note: A take can run for the full film, but the domain stops at 600 s.

colour_temperature.note: One white balance holds for the whole shot.

sources.title: David Bordwell, The Way Hollywood Tells It: Story and Style in Modern Movies (University of California Press, 2006)
